text:
maria: morning team — handing off the 06:00->14:00 shift. Quick summary of overnight and current state below, please read and ack.

incident-bot: PAGE triggered at 02:47 UTC — kv-cache pressure detected on pool-4; 503 rate increased to ~4% for 20m. Auto-fallback to smaller shard happened at 02:55.

maria: timeline: 02:47 alert for elevated queue length on pool-4 (nv8a). 02:50 first customer reports (chat timeouts). 02:55 autoscaler performed shard fallback; 03:05 we applied temp cache eviction tweak, 03:12 reduced 503s to ~0.5%. Full mitigations in progress.

aj: adding notes from the on-call rotation — metric to watch is inference.request_queue_len and kv_store.evictions_per_min. We saw evictions spike right before 02:47.

kevin: root cause hypothesis — a hot prefix pattern from a scheduled analytics job caused disproportionate KV lookups and hit the hot-key path. That overloaded the KV cache memory working set and triggered eviction/backpressure.

maria: customer impact — scoped: 10% of requests to the affected model variant got 5xx/503 during the peak window (02:47-03:05). A handful of customers reported elevated error rates (CS ticket #C-2319 opened). No SLA breach yet but close.

sasha: FYI, one enterprise workspace had a burst that coincided with their nightly report. I'm pinging their AMs.

aj: mitigations taken overnight (concrete):
- toggled autoscale policy to add 2 nodes to pool-4 at 02:52 (`/infra autoscale add --pool pool-4 --count 2`).
- enabled aggressive prefix-eviction (temporary) at 03:05 (`/kv tune --policy prefix_eviction:aggressive`).
- rolled the model variant to quantized fallback for hot-shard at 03:18 (no code change).
Result: errors down to baseline by 03:22.

kevin: permanent next steps we started: add hotkey sharding rule for analytics job, increase kv cache headroom for pool-4 by 25%, and add a circuit-breaker to reject >200 qps from a single API key to protect pool.

maria: current status (as of handoff):
- incident state: resolved (monitoring).
- active alerts: none firing at pagerduty threshold; infra metrics still show slightly elevated evictions (~3/min) on pool-4.
- customer impact: CS tickets created and flagged high-priority, retries recommended for customers who saw 503s.

aj: coverage / gaps for my shift: primary/secondary pair is maria/aj for next 8 hours. Kevin is reachable for escalation until 10:00 UTC. No on-call overlap scheduled from 11:00-12:00 UTC — please treat as potential coverage gap, we should have someone in rotation for that window if we expect more churn.

maria: runbook pointers (shortcuts):
- KV cache pressure runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-pressure
- Quick mitigation CLI: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/ops-cli#kv-tune (commands above).
- If paging again, follow the 'hotkey isolation' section first, then 'node autoscale' if latency doesn't recover in 3m.

kevin: debugging tips if it pages again: run `rbx metrics query "kv_store.evictions_per_min{pool='pool-4'}"` and `rbx traces query --prefix hotkey` to find offending prefixes. Use `rbx kv shard-assign --dry-run` before applying sharding rules.

maria: requests for the next shift (aj): please keep an eye on pool-4 evictions and the customer CS queue. If evictions > 10/min and errors >1% for >5m, escalate to kevin and open an incident channel with `incident-bot create --sev 2`.

aj: acked. I'll also put a short watch alert for the 11:00-12:00 gap and ask infra to cover the window.

maria: any other notes? otherwise I'm handing off to aj. :coffee:

kevin: small note — we'll sprint the hotkey detection job today (estimated 4h). If you see repeating patterns, tag them with `hotkey:analytics` so we can auto-block.

aj: closing ack from me — thanks all, will keep the channel updated on any paging.

incident-bot: Incident channel archived. Summary attached to ticket C-2319.
